items.title: Zanetor Rawlings could be moved in bigger Cabinet reshuffle – Nitiwul
items.description: Former Defence Minister says newly appointed Minister for Environment, Science and Technology, Dr Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings, could be reassigned if President John Dramani Mahama carries out what he described as a broader Cabinet reshuffle later this year. Speaking on The Pulse on JoyNews on Friday, August 7, while discussing President Mahama’s recent ministerial changes, Dominic Nitiwul said he was not surprised by Dr Zanetor Rawlings’ appointment but believes she is better suited for a different ministry. He disclosed that Dr Rawlings had previously been considered for a ministerial position even before her latest appointment. “I think that even the first time that she was not made a minister, she was supposed to be made a Minister of State in one of the ministries. I will not mention because it will be too obvious.” According to Mr Nitiwul, her appointment to the Environment, Science and Technology Ministry did not come as a surprise. “So I’m not surprised that they’re sticking her there.” However, he suggested that her current role may only be temporary. “I think that when the President wants to do a proper reshuffle that the country is expecting, I expect her to move. Everybody knows the ministry that she will fit in, so I expect that she will move.” Mr Nitiwul said that many Ghanaians had expected a more extensive reshuffle and said public pressure on the President to reorganise his government continues to grow. “The country is demanding the reshuffle. The country is saying that a lot of the ministers are not performing.” “Even the NDC people are mentioning names that the people are not performing, they need to be removed, and they are surprised,” he added. According to the former Defence Minister, many expected President Mahama to replace more ministers during the latest changes. “People are really surprised that the President has not done any reshuffle because it was obvious that the President was going to take out a lot.” Mr Nitiwul, however, acknowledged that removing ministers who are also Members of Parliament presents political challenges. “It’s very difficult to reshuffle a Member of Parliament and ask him to go and sit in Parliament, without giving him any position.” He said President Mahama is now facing the same dilemma that confronted previous administrations. “They were going after President Akufo-Addo, saying he didn’t do reshuffles. But I’m sure he’s now learned the hard lesson that removing a Member of Parliament completely and asking him to go and sit in Parliament, you find that his political career is blown away.” Mr Nitiwul added that the President’s own appointments have made any future reshuffle more difficult. “He has entangled himself. He’s the one who has done his appointment. So we are all waiting.” Despite the challenges, he believes another Cabinet reshuffle is inevitable and warned that delaying it could create problems within the governing party. “The country is demanding a reshuffle. And trust me, if he doesn’t do a reshuffle before the end of this year, he’s going to get a lot of problems, not even from the opposition like us, but from his own party.” Mr Nitiwul reiterated his expectation that Dr Zanetor Rawlings would be reassigned when those changes are made. “I am clear in my mind that by the time we do that reshuffle, they might move Zanetor Rawlings to a more appropriate ministry.” President John Dramani Mahama has earlier today nominated Klottey Korle Member of Parliament, Dr Zanetor Agyemang-Rawlings, as Minister for Environment, Science and Technology , as part of a cabinet shake-up aimed at filling key government positions.

items.title: Galamsey now threatening food supply chain, pushing up prices – Agricultural Advocates Warn
items.description: Ghana’s illegal mining crisis is no longer only about polluted rivers and destroyed forests. Agricultural advocates say the activities of galamsey operators are now threatening the country’s food supply chain by reducing farmland, cutting production, and pushing up the prices consumers pay at markets. The Chief Executive Officer of The Ghanaian Farmer, Enyonam Manye, says the destruction of fertile agricultural lands is creating a supply challenge that is gradually translating into higher food prices for households. “When people hear the word galamsey, they immediately think about polluted rivers, destroyed forests and illegal mining. While those who are serious or those who are concerned, there’s another consequence that affects every Ghanaian every single day, is the rising cost of food,” she said. According to her, farms that once produced essential crops including vegetables, maize, cassava, plantain, and cocoa are being lost to illegal mining activities, reducing the amount of food available for the local market. “Across many parts of Ghana, productive farms that are used to grow cocoa, vegetables, maize, cassava, plantain have been excavated by illegal miners,” Enyonam Manye stated. She explained that the reduction in farmland means farmers are unable to maintain previous levels of production, creating shortages that eventually affect prices. “Every acre of farmland lost means food entering our markets. When supplies fall down, that means that the demand of food will become high and it will have shot the price because more lands have been destroyed,” she added. The agricultural advocate said many farmers are also losing access to land because some landowners are choosing financial gains from illegal mining over farming activities. “When your family gets big money and they decide to let go of their land to Galamsey people… whatever you use to farm on, if it’s a five acre or 10 acre, you will be left with either half or quarter of that,” she said. For consumers, she noted that the impact is eventually felt at markets where traders factor in additional costs before setting prices. “The market will be forced to charge for transportation and charge for many other things. So at the end of the day, we the consumers end up paying higher because of the distraction that is being caused to our farmlands,” she explained. JoyNews Data and Research Analyst, Maxwell Aklorbortu, said the relationship between illegal mining and rising food prices can be explained through the basic economics of supply and demand. He noted that contamination of farmland and water sources forces farmers to reduce production, abandon farms, or spend more resources to continue farming elsewhere. “Once the farmland and irrigation water becomes contaminated, farmers either harvest less, abandon their farms altogether, or incur additional costs just to move production elsewhere,” Maxwell said. “Reduced food production means lower supply. And we know these are simple economies. If supply is less and the demand is high, prices are forced to push up,” he added. The Ghana Youth Environmental Movement (GEM) also highlighted how galamsey is affecting farming communities, citing the example of Isiakwa in the Eastern Region. National Coordinator of GEM, Glory Emmanuella Appiah, said the community once produced much of its own food but has now become dependent on supplies from elsewhere after farmlands were converted into mining sites. “Isiakwa used to be a farming community where they grew their own food. So they grew their cassava, their plantains. But because of the rising interest in Galamsey by some of the young people, some of the young people were selling their farmlands,” she said. She added that once food has to be brought in from other communities, prices often rise because sellers take advantage of the increased demand. “People were no longer growing their food themselves. And so if other people from other towns brought in the foodstuff, they mentioned the prices that they wanted for the foodstuff,” she explained. The speakers warned that without urgent measures to protect agricultural lands and address illegal mining, Ghana risks worsening food affordability challenges and weakening its long-term food security. The government has previously announced various interventions to combat illegal mining, including Operation Halt and the deployment of military personnel to mining sites. However, advocates argue that more comprehensive action is needed to protect farmlands and prevent the destruction of agricultural livelihoods. The Ministry of Food and Agriculture is yet to respond to the concerns raised by agricultural advocates regarding the impact of galamsey on food production and prices.

items.title: Gloria Boye-Doku launches two books to inspire young people to rise above their backgrounds
items.description: Partner, Tax and Regulatory at Deloitte Ghana, Gloria Boye-Doku, has launched two new books titled “Mindset for Success” and “The Power of Hope” aimed at inspiring young people to believe that their background should never limit their aspirations. Speaking at the book launch held at the British Council in Accra, she said the publication was motivated by conversations she regularly has with students through her mentorship engagements with institutions including UPSA, Accra Technical University and other schools. According to her, many students mistakenly believe successful people achieve their dreams because they were born into privileged circumstances. “This book is to tell them that no matter your background, no matter where you are coming from, the most important thing is your mindset. And with the right mindset, your background is not a limitation. You can aspire to whatever height and you can achieve success,” she said. She further encouraged readers not to allow a lack of resources or difficult circumstances to prevent them from pursuing their goals. “Your background has no role to play in your success journey. You just have to know that you are capable. I believe readers will be motivated and not held back by their background or lack of resources. That shouldn’t be a limiting factor,” she added. Renowned Ghanaian playwright and author, Uncle Ebo Whyte commended Madam Boye-Doku for documenting her personal experiences and making them available to inspire others. He described the book as an investment in future generations rather than leaving behind untold stories. “Gloria has paid her dues. She hasn’t left a debt for her grandchildren to come and pay. Indeed, she’s making an investment for her grandchildren to come and be blessed by,” he said. The book is expected to motivate students, professionals and aspiring leaders by demonstrating that success is shaped more by determination, resilience and mindset than by one’s background.

Rappelant que cette formation va au-delà du cadre scolaire traditionnel, le ministre a affirmé que l'avenir du pays repose sur le terrain de la responsabilité citoyenne. Le gouvernement, a-t-il précisé, entend façonner des citoyens « hautement qualifiés », dotés avant tout d’un « cœur patriotique ». Il s’est dit vivement encouragé par la visite des autorités gouvernementales. items.title: Security in Northern Ghana must be a top priority for new Defence Minister – Security analyst
items.description: Security analyst Dr Victor Doke has urged the newly assigned Defence Minister, Kenneth Gilbert Adjei, to make security in Northern Ghana his immediate priority. He stressed the need to strengthen border protection, improve intelligence capabilities and deepen collaboration among the country’s security agencies. Speaking on JoyNews’ The Pulse on Friday, August 7, Dr Doke said the minister’s success would largely depend on his ability to equip the security services with the resources needed to combat emerging threats, particularly violent extremism along Ghana’s northern frontier. “Apart from what we’ve talked about with regards to the northern borders, enhancing capability and providing resources for the men in uniform to use is very important,” he said. According to him, adequately resourcing the security services would significantly improve intelligence gathering and strengthen efforts to counter violent extremist activities. “Availability of resources would mean that you have success in intelligence gathering and in countering violent extremism,” he stated. Dr Doke also called for stronger coordination between the Defence Ministry, the Interior Ministry, the National Security Secretariat and other security institutions in tackling the country’s internal security challenges. He cited the late Defence Minister, Dr Edward Omane Boamah, as an example of the collaborative approach required, particularly in efforts to address the protracted conflict in Bawku. “We know what the late Dr Omane Boamah did with regards to the Bawku crisis. Contributions of ideas and coordinating with other security agencies are very key,” he said. The security analyst noted that beyond being visible in office, the new minister must provide strategic leadership by offering practical ideas and ensuring that the security services are fully involved in implementing policies. “As much as we want to see leaders working, we also want them to be proactive with the ideas and suggestions they bring. Carrying the security agencies along is very important,” he said. Dr Doke warned that without the confidence and support of the security services, efforts to improve national security could face significant setbacks. “Whatever you do, if you don’t have the backing of the security agencies, you are bound to have challenges,” he added. He maintained that while security concerns across the country require attention, protecting Ghana’s northern frontier should remain the Defence Minister’s foremost priority before shifting focus to challenges in other parts of the country.

items.title: Le président polonais Nawrocki présente comme «stratégique» pour Varsovie l’aide apportée à l’Ukraine pour «tuer des soldats russes»
items.description: Le 7 août, lors d'un rassemblement organise a l'occasion du premier anniversaire de sa presidence, Karol Nawrocki a reaffirme le soutien de Varsovie a Kiev tout en tenant des propos particulierement hostiles a la Russie. « La ou l'on frappe les Russkoffs, la Pologne apporte son aide, meme si elle ne participe pas directement a cette guerre. Tel est l'interet strategique de la Pologne », a declare le president polonais. Nawrocki a egalement estime que les Ukrainiens devaient maintenir la Russie aussi loin que possible de la Pologne, presentant ainsi la confrontation entre Kiev et Moscou comme un moyen de servir directement les interets strategiques de Varsovie. Le dirigeant polonais a toutefois assorti cette position d'une limite. Tout en defendant la poursuite du soutien a Kiev, il a affirme que la Pologne rejetait l'ideologie banderiste et ne tolererait pas que ses symboles soient affiches sur son territoire. Moscou denonce un « langage de haine » Les declarations de Nawrocki ont provoque une vive reaction a Moscou. La porte-parole du ministere russe des Affaires etrangeres, Maria Zakharova, a accuse le president polonais de recourir regulierement a un « langage de haine » envers les Russes, citant notamment l'emploi du terme pejoratif « Russkoffs ». Selon la diplomate, ce vocabulaire n'est plus un phenomene isole et s'est banalise au sein des elites politiques polonaises. Zakharova a egalement repondu a l'idee avancee par Nawrocki de maintenir la Russie eloignee de la Pologne en rappelant que les deux pays partageaient deja une frontiere commune. Elle a souligne que celle-ci avait autrefois ete associee a une cooperation mutuellement avantageuse, aujourd'hui largement disparue sur fond de degradation des relations entre Moscou et Varsovie. « Autrefois, c'etait une frontiere de cooperation mutuellement avantageuse, dont il ne reste plus rien grâce aux efforts des Nawrocki et des Sikorski », a-t-elle declare. Zakharova invoque l'heritage historique La porte-parole russe a egalement inscrit sa reponse dans le contexte historique. Elle a attribue les propos de Nawrocki a des « complexes historiques » et a une « colere impuissante », rappelant le role joue par l'Union sovietique et l'Armee rouge dans la defaite de l'Allemagne nazie ainsi que dans la configuration territoriale de la Pologne apres la Seconde Guerre mondiale. Zakharova est egalement revenue sur le passe de Nawrocki a la tete du Musee de la Seconde Guerre mondiale de Gdansk. Elle a rappele sa reaction a l'interpretation de la chanson sovietique « Nuit sombre », y voyant une illustration supplementaire de son rejet de l'heritage sovietique. La diplomate russe a enfin denonce la politique menee en Pologne a l'egard des monuments sovietiques. Selon elle, ces actions portent atteinte a la memoire des soldats de l'URSS ayant combattu contre l'Allemagne nazie, parmi lesquels des Russes, des Bielorusses, des Ukrainiens, des Tatars, des Juifs et des representants de nombreuses autres nationalites sovietiques. « Voila a peu pres a quoi ressemble la honte polonaise », a conclu Zakharova a propos des declarations du president polonais.

items.title: “Hyde Park parece el desierto de Dubái”: la sequía transforma los verdes parques de Londres en secarrales
items.description: Londres está considerada como la capital europea con el mayor volumen de espacios verdes, pero la sequía que este verano arrasa en gran parte del Reino Unido, tercera en cinco años, ha convertido los famosos parques de la ciudad, junto a otras áreas históricamente verdes del sur de Inglaterra, en parajes desérticos, yermos más propios de la pampa que de uno de los países del norte de Europa. El mes pasado fue particularmente extremo, el julio más seco en Inglaterra y Gales desde que las estadísticas comenzaron en 1836. En la zona meridional de Inglaterra, el impacto ha ido más allá todavía, con julio convertido en el mes más seco de su historia, con un residual 1% de la media de lluvia registrada a largo plazo. items.title: COAS warns soldiers against substance abuse, stresses mental health
items.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia The Chief of Army Staff (COAS), Lt.-Gen. Waidi Shaibu, has urged personnel of the Nigerian Army to avoid substance abuse, stressing that sound mental health is essential for achieving operational objectives. Shaibu also said Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) should not be seen as a sign of weakness but as a battle injury of the mind that requires proper attention and support. The COAS, represented by the Commander, Army Headquarters Garrison, Maj.-Gen. John Lar, stated this on Wednesday during a four-day sensitisation seminar held at the Headquarters of 4 Special Forces, Doma, Nasarawa State. “I want to reiterate that post-traumatic stress disorder is not a sign of weakness; it is a battle injury of the mind. We are committed to providing the necessary support system, early intervention and professional counselling to help our warriors transition successfully from trauma to triumph,” he said. The Army chief warned that substance abuse among troops would not be tolerated, describing it as a major threat to combat readiness, unit cohesion and operational effectiveness. “I urge commanders at all levels to intensify the fight against this menace within our barracks and formations,” he said. The seminar, titled “Transformational Leadership, Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder and Drugs/Substance Abuse,” was organised by the Department of Army Transformation and Innovation. Shaibu said the programme was designed to build trust, inspire troops through shared vision and empower personnel to adapt to unpredictable operational environments. He added that the initiative was part of ongoing efforts by the Nigerian Army to sensitise junior and mid-level officers on effective leadership practices and values required for successful command. “The seminar focuses on three very critical pillars of modern military operations: transformational leadership, management of post-traumatic stress disorder and the devastating effects of drugs and substance abuse,” he said. According to him, the changing nature of security threats facing the country requires a professional, resilient and psychologically sound military force. He urged junior and mid-level commanders to embrace transformational leadership by not only giving orders but also inspiring, mentoring and caring for the welfare of their subordinates. The COAS commended troops for their loyalty and commitment, particularly their efforts in tackling security challenges in North Central Nigeria. Also speaking, the Chief of Transformation and Innovation, Maj.-Gen. Peter Okoye, described the seminar as timely, given the physical and psychological demands of modern military operations. Okoye said the programme aligned with the COAS Command Philosophy of transforming the Nigerian Army into a more professional, adaptable, combat-ready and resilient force. “The strength of the Nigerian Army lies not only in its equipment and capabilities but also in the resilience, discipline and mental readiness of its personnel,” he said. He added that as the Army continues to record successes in training and operations, there was a need to sustain efforts aimed at improving leadership quality, mental health, troop cohesion and operational efficiency. items.title: Bignona : les pépinières inondent le marché
items.description: À Bignona, les pépinières d’arbres fruitiers inondent les abords du marché. Les pépiniéristes qui viennent de l’intérieur du département, particulièrement de la zone de Kafountine, se frottent les mains. BIGNONA – On les aperçoit voltigeant sur les porte-bagages des voitures individuelles ou de transport en commun, des bicyclettes, des tricycles, etc. Leurs destinations sont inconnues, mais une bonne partie se retrouve au marché de Bignona. Ici, les plants inondent l’un des abords de la Route nationale 4 (Rn4). Avec des mottes de terre humide témoignant de l’origine des sols argileux d’où ils sont arrachés, des orangers de différentes variétés, des manguiers greffés ou ordinaires, des goyaviers, des corossoliers, des fleurs d’embellissement…longent la route. D’autres sont encore dans leurs sachets noirs remplis de terre. Ceux qui s’activent dans ce commerce viennent de contrées lointaines. « Je viens de Kounkoudiang. Ces plants proviennent de mon jardin. J’avais amené 400 pieds, mais il ne m’en reste que 150 », déclare Moussa Kambaye avec joie, indexant le reste de sa production. « Nous vendons les orangers à 1.500 FCfa et les manguiers à 2.000 FCfa. Ces derniers prennent du temps, alors qu’un an suffit pour les orangers. Mais, tout dépend de l’engrais. Nous utilisons de l’engrais organique, du fumier », explique ce ressortissant guinéen avec beaucoup de peine. La période tout comme l’endroit choisi pour exposer ces semis sont stratégiques. A lire aussi : Reboisement: 400 cocotiers plantés au camp militaire de Bignona La Rn4 est incontournable pour rallier Ziguinchor, la capitale régionale, et la Guinée-Bissau, alors que la même route mène à la frontière avec la République sœur de Gambie. C’est aussi un carrefour pour aller jusqu’au nord du pays. « Cela fait quatre années que je viens vendre ici à la même période ; l’activité marche très bien », confesse Yancouba, lui aussi pépiniériste d’origine guinéenne, basé à Kounkoudiang, un village frontalier de la Gambie, dans la commune de Kataba 1. Seydou Bodian, un habitant de Nématoulaye, quartier de la commune de Tenghory, vient d’acheter trois orangers greffés. Cet enseignant a rappelé l’importance d’avoir des arbres fruitiers à domicile. « C’est pour remplacer les anacardiers que j’ai coupé pour construire la maison. Les plants assurent la sécurité alimentaire et l’ombrage ; ce qui peut contribuer à retenir les enfants à la maison et leur éviter d’aller voler des fruits chez les voisins. Aussi, une demeure avec des arbres fruitiers est toujours fréquentée », explique M. Bodian, la cinquantaine révolue. « C’est également pour protéger les maisons contre les tempêtes », poursuit notre interlocuteur. Il préfère les plants greffés, car les ordinaires, dit-il, demandent beaucoup plus de temps avant de commencer à produire. Une bonne affaire pour les revendeurs « Pourtant, ils résistent mieux au vent. En plus, leurs fleurons ne tombent pas comme pour les greffés », explique un autre client parti à la hâte après avoir payé une vingtaine de pieds. « Les catégories courtes produisent plus vite, mais sont difficiles à entretenir », renchérit M. Bodian. Revendeuse, Lucie Diatta est ravie d’en savoir plus sur les plants. Elle dit apprendre des techniques et savoir-faire de ses clients. La jeune dame s’est lancée dans cette activité depuis trois ans. Mais, la vente des pépinières n’est qu’une alternative pour elle. Pâtissière de formation, Lucie dite Mme Diatta troque son tablier pour mettre des bottes et des gangs afin de devenir vendeuse de pépinières entre juillet et août. « Mes clients viennent de partout. J’en ai jusqu’en Guinée-Bissau », se vante la jeune dame au commerce facile, la taille moyenne et le teint noir. Ses plants lui viennent de Birassou, un village de la commune de Kataba 1, département de Bignona. À l’en croire, l’activité est lucrative. Elle achète le pied à 1.000 FCfa et le revend à 1.500 FCfa. « J’arrive vraiment à satisfaire mes besoins sans l’aide de personne », confie Lucie. Fatou Dominos Sané dite Méra vient elle aussi de Kounkoudiang pour vendre ses pépinières d’arbres fruitiers. Elle expose sur la chaussée de la Rn4 des pieds de manguiers, de corossoliers, de citronniers et de goyaviers. Mère et soutien de famille, elle a commencé par vendre des légumes au village, puis des noix de cajou et autres marchandises. Ce business lui a permis de disposer d’une superficie où elle entretient ses plants. Aujourd’hui, elle est devenue une pépiniériste. « Pourtant, j’ai eu le bac littéraire, mais j’ai perdu mes diplômes. Alors je suis retournée travailler la terre jusqu’à avoir un jardin 50/50. J’y travaille depuis quatre ans », raconte-t-elle. Par Kadidiatou SONKO (Correspondante)

items.title: Il tue son frère au cours d’une altercation
items.description: La Police sénégalaise a annoncé, ce vendredi 7 août 2026, l'interpellation d'un homme soupçonné d'avoir mortellement poignardé son frère à l'issue d'une bagarre survenue à Guinaw Rails. L'information qui a été publiée par l'institution policière sur sa page Facebook, précise que le suspect a été placé en garde à vue tandis que les investigations se poursuivent. Le Commissariat d'arrondissement de Guinaw Rail au Sénégal, a procédé, le 6 août 2026, à l'arrestation d'un individu poursuivi pour «coups et blessures volontaires» ayant entraîné la mort, a indiqué la Police sénégalaise dans une publication diffusée, ce vendredi 7 août sur sa page Facebook. Les faits se sont déroulés le jeudi 6 août aux environs de 19 h 30. Alertés à la suite d'une rixe ayant coûté la vie à un charretier résidant à Guinaw Rails, les policiers de la brigade de Police judiciaire se sont rapidement rendus sur les lieux. Sur place, ils ont découvert le corps sans vie de la victime, baignant dans son sang, dans la cour de la concession familiale située à Guinaw-Rails Sud, dans le quartier Ousmane Mbengue. Les premiers témoignages recueillis auprès des personnes présentes ont révélé que la victime s'était «violemment disputée» avec son jeune frère. Au cours de l'affrontement, ce dernier lui aurait porté un coup de couteau fatal. Après le constat d'usage, les Sapeurs-pompiers ont évacué le corps vers la morgue de l'hôpital de Pikine, où une autopsie doit être pratiquée afin de déterminer avec précision les causes du décès. Les investigations menées par les enquêteurs ont permis d'identifier le suspect, qui avait pris la fuite après les faits. Il a finalement été localisé puis interpellé à proximité du stade Alassane Djigo. Entendu par les enquêteurs, le mis en cause a reconnu avoir porté le coup de couteau. Il a toutefois affirmé avoir agi en réaction aux violences physiques exercées par son frère au cours d'un corps-à-corps. Placée en garde à vue, la personne interpellée reste à la disposition de la justice. La Police sénégalaise précise que l'enquête se poursuit afin d'établir l'ensemble des circonstances ayant conduit à ce drame familial. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Il tue son frère au cours d’une altercation est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Kano rejects conversion of Jambulo afforestation complex to private plots
items.description: By Hadiza Yusuf The Kano State Government has rejected any move to convert parts of the historic Afforestation Programme Coordinating Unit (APCU) complex in Jambulo into private residential or commercial plots, insisting that the facility must remain for public environmental purposes. The state Commissioner for Water Resources, Environment and Climate Change, Dr Dahir M. Hashim, stated this on Friday while addressing journalists in Kano. Hashim described the complex as an important federal environmental facility that has played a key role in coordinating afforestation activities and training forestry personnel. He said the government was concerned by reports that portions of the property had allegedly been allocated to private interests and that there were attempts to remove federal environmental agencies operating from the facility. “The APCU complex was established in 1988 and has, for decades, served as a centre for coordinating afforestation activities and training forest guards and other forestry personnel,” he said. According to the commissioner, the facility should not be regarded as abandoned government property, particularly following the relocation of the operational headquarters of the National Agency for the Great Green Wall (NAGGW) from Abuja to Jambulo. “The Kano State Government respects the authority of the courts and will not interfere with the judicial process. However, any attempt to convert this strategic environmental facility into private residential or commercial plots is against the overriding public interest,” Hashim said. He stressed the environmental significance of the complex, noting that its mature trees help reduce heat, improve air quality, prevent erosion and support biodiversity. Hashim warned that the destruction or fragmentation of the green area would result in the loss of vegetation that had taken decades to develop. He called on President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice to review the reported alienation of the property and take appropriate legal steps to protect the entire complex. The commissioner also urged the Federal Ministry of Environment to continue opposing any attempt to alienate the property and explore available legal options to preserve the facility. He said the Kano State Government was prepared to support the Federal Ministry of Environment, NAGGW, the National Environmental Standards and Regulations Enforcement Agency (NESREA) and APCU in safeguarding the complex. “Our position is clear: public environmental assets must remain in public service,” Hashim said. The post Kano rejects conversion of Jambulo afforestation complex to private plots appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Niger : la Commission de lutte contre la corruption a recouvré 74 milliards de francs CFA depuis sa création
items.description: Creee en septembre 2023, la Commission nigerienne de lutte contre la delinquance economique, financiere et fiscale (COLDEFF) a annonce le 5 août avoir recouvre environ 12 milliards de francs CFA (soit un peu plus de 21 millions de dollars) durant les onze a douze derniers mois, portant le montant total des sommes recuperees a 74 milliards de francs CFA (soit environ 130 millions de dollars) depuis son entree en service. C'est ce qui ressort des declarations du president de la Commission, le colonel Zennou Moussa Aghali, lors d'une conference de presse, tenue a l'issue de sa reunion avec le chef de l'etat, dans laquelle il a egalement fait savoir que les sommes recuperees correspondaient exclusivement a des liquidites. « C'est le recouvrement en cash, il n'y a pas d'actions, il n'y a pas de biens immobiliers, c'est du numeraire », a precise le chef de la COLDEFF. Zennou Moussa Aghali a indique que les fonds recouvres incluaient des recouvrements en especes, par cheques, par virements bancaires, ainsi qu'au titre de compensations en nature. Avant le dernier recouvrement, l'institution avait cumule 63 milliards de francs CFA (soit un peu plus de 110 millions de dollars). Recouvrement dans le « respect », tout en restant « ferme » Concernant son audience avec le chef de l'etat, Abdourahamane Tiani, Zennou Moussa Aghali a declare qu'il avait recu la demande de poursuivre l'engagement de la Commission pour le recouvrement des avoirs dissipes de l'etat dans le « respect », mais tout en restant « ferme » avec les mis en cause, rappelant que « la sanction de la COLDEFF, c'est la sanction pecuniaire ». Il convient de noter que, selon un communique officiel du gouvernement, la COLDEFF est munie de « tous les pouvoirs necessaires pour mettre en œuvre les orientations du Conseil national pour la sauvegarde de la patrie (CNSP) et du gouvernement, relatives a la lutte contre la delinquance economique, financiere et fiscale, dans le respect des lois et reglements de la Republique ». Les autorites nigeriennes affirment que les fonds recuperes par la COLDEFF seront reinjectes dans les finances publiques et dans les projets de developpement national.

items.title: Italy defies Spanish demand to lift border curbs over Ceuta migrant crisis
items.description: Spain threatened on Friday to impose restrictions on travellers from Italy unless Rome lifts by Sunday the border controls it introduced last week following a mass influx of migrants into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta. Italy swiftly responded, saying it would not accept “ultimatums or impositions” from Madrid, adding that it would keep in place its suspension of Schengen rules for non-EU nationals arriving from Spain until at least August 15. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni’s conservative government had previously said the more robust travel checks would remain in force until the end of the month. The Spanish government said Italy’s decision to reintroduce controls on arrivals from Spain was “unjustified, contrary to the interests of the European Union and discriminatory against the Spanish population”. It promised to adopt “proportionate measures” against Italy unless Meloni rolled back the new constraints by Sunday. However, in a toughly worded statement, Meloni’s office said Spanish authorities had themselves warned of a new migrant influx into Ceuta on August 15. It said it would only reconsider its decision once it was certain there was no new migration wave, no security or terrorism risk to Italy and no irregular migrants heading towards European territory. Spain’s Civil Guard has said it is aware of calls online for a fresh border crossing attempt at Ceuta on August 15, however it is not clear how many people might take part. Spain accuses Italy of ignoring facts As many as 72,000 people rushed to cross the border last week and dozens died in the attempt. Most have since returned to neighbouring Morocco but hundreds of unaccompanied minors remain in Ceuta. Italy, which does not share a land border with Spain, justified its decision to partially suspend the EU’s border-free Schengen arrangements to prevent any of the migrants who entered Ceuta from travelling to Italy. There has been no indication that any of them want to travel to Italy, or have the money to pay for an airline ticket. Madrid said the Italian move was based on “spurious arguments” that lacked any factual basis because the migrants who entered Ceuta irregularly could not gain access to the Schengen area. Italy and Spain split on migration policy The dispute between the two EU allies marks a new low in relations between the right-winger Meloni, and Spain’s Socialist prime minister, Pedro Sanchez. Meloni has positioned herself as one of Europe’s leading advocates of tighter immigration controls, while Sanchez has generally defended a more liberal approach and recently backed a large-scale regularisation programme for undocumented migrants. “I think what were saying is reasonable. What doesn’t hold water at all is Italy’s stance towards Spain. The impression is that Ms Meloni is on a crusade,” Spain’s Youth Minister Sira Rego told Spanish public broadcaster TVE1 . In Friday’s statement, the Spanish government said Italy had registered the highest number of “irregular crossings in recent years”, with figures that have been double those of Spain.

items.title: Man City reject Barcelona bid for Rodri – Reports
items.description: Manchester City have reportedly rejected an opening bid of £38.5 million ($52 million) from Barcelona for World Cup winner Rodri. The 30-year-old has just one season remaining on his deal at the Etihad Stadium and has been strongly linked with a return to his native Spain. City are understood to want about £68 million for Rodri, who was named player of the tournament at the recent World Cup in North America. Real Madrid had appeared likely to be Rodri’s next club, but La Liga rivals Barcelona now seem to be in pole position. Rodri joined City from Atletico Madrid in 2019 and won multiple Premier League titles and the 2023 Champions League under former boss Pep Guardiola. He won Euro 2024 and that year’s Ballon d’Or before a serious knee injury ruled him out of much of the 2024/25 campaign. AFP The post Man City reject Barcelona bid for Rodri – Reports appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 2027: Youths, students rally behind Tinubu, Abiodun, Adeola in Ogun
items.description: By Henry Ojelu Hundreds of youths and students yesterday staged a solidarity trek in Abeokuta, Ogun State, declaring support for President Bola Tinubu, Governor Dapo Abiodun and Senator Solomon Olamilekan Adeola (Yayi) ahead of the 2027 general elections. The rally, organised by the Yayi Progressives Movement, saw participants march through major streets of the state capital after converging at the MKO Abiola International Stadium, Kuto, carrying banners and placards while chanting slogans in support of the three All Progressives Congress, APC, leaders. Addressing participants at the Ake Palace, the Convener of the movement, Engr. Armstrong ‘Tope Akintunde, said the solidarity trek was organised to demonstrate support for President Tinubu’s expected second-term bid, Governor Abiodun’s reported senatorial ambition and Senator Adeola’s governorship aspiration in Ogun State. Akintunde said the mobilisation was inspired by what the group described as the economic reforms of the Tinubu administration, as well as the developmental and empowerment programmes of Governor Abiodun and Senator Adeola. According to him, the initiative was also aimed at encouraging youths to participate actively in the democratic process while reaffirming their commitment to the APC. He commended Senator Adeola for his contributions to youth empowerment and infrastructure development across the state. “We have every reason to support our principals because we are confident that, come 2027, they will record a landslide victory. Over the past three years, President Tinubu’s reforms and Senator Yayi’s track record in empowerment, infrastructure development and constituency projects have continued to inspire many young people to support their leadership,” Akintunde said. Also speaking, Co-Convener of the movement and former member of the House of Representatives, Kehinde Odeneye, described the solidarity trek as peaceful and orderly. Odeneye said the exercise reflected the commitment of the movement’s youth and student wings to promoting unity, political participation and greater engagement within the APC. “The Youth and Students Wings of the movement have conducted this peaceful and orderly exercise under our supervision. This initiative promotes unity, encourages active political participation and strengthens youth engagement within the All Progressives Congress in Ogun State. “We also want the public to know that we remain firmly aligned with our leaders and fully support the position expressed by our Convener. They have consistently demonstrated exemplary leadership, and we are pleased to organise this exercise in support of their vision as preparations for the 2027 general elections gather momentum,” he said. items.title: GSA begins nationwide sensitisation for shippers
items.description: The Ghana Shippers’ Authority (GSA) has begun a nationwide sensitisation of shippers on the mandatory registration of shippers on the Integrated Customs Management System (ICUMS) in accordance with the Ghana Shippers’ Authority Act, 2024 (Act 1122). Officials of the GSA, the Customs Division of the Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA), and ICUMS have toured the country to explain how the electronic system will ease cargo clearance and support the collection of data for policy formulation and adjustments. On Wednesday, 5th August 2026, a sensitisation program was organised for executives of Freight Forwarding Associations at the Ghana Shippers’ House. The engagement was aimed at promoting compliance with Section 26(1) of Act 1122, which requires all importers and exporters to register with the Authority before processing shipment transactions through the ICUMS platform. Opening the programme, the Deputy Chief Executive Officer in charge of Technical Services, Mrs. Sylvia Asana Dauda Owu, underscored the importance of the mandatory registration and urged freight forwarders to support the process by ensuring that their clients registered to avoid disruptions to cargo clearance. Officials of the GSA and Ghana Link Network Services Ltd. subsequently demonstrated the ICUMS registration process and responded to stakeholders’ questions to facilitate a smooth implementation. During the discussions, freight forwarders appealed for the implementation deadline to be extended to Monday to 31st August 2026, to allow additional time for stakeholder sensitisation and compliance. Mrs. Dauda Owu acknowledged the request and assured participants that Management would consider the appeal and communicate its decision. The meeting also addressed the implementation of the Container Administrative Charge (CAC). The President of the Ghana Institute of Freight Forwarders (GIFF), Mr. Stephen Adjokatcher, and the Chairman of the GIFF Tema Chapter, Mr. Johnny Mantey, encouraged freight forwarders to ensure that importers complied with the approved GH¢720 Container Administrative Charge, emphasising the need for industry-wide support. Also addressing the meeting, the Deputy Commissioner of the Customs Division of the Ghana Revenue Authority, Mr. Divine Agbeko, called for continued collaboration among stakeholders to facilitate seamless cargo clearance and improve trade efficiency. The engagement forms part of the Authority’s ongoing efforts to strengthen regulatory compliance, enhance stakeholder collaboration, and promote efficient trade through the effective implementation of Act 1122 (2024).

items.title: Court fixes August 31 for judgment in Shinkafi’s suit against APC, INEC
items.description: By Idris Salisu, Gusau A Federal High Court sitting in Gusau, Zamfara State, has fixed August 31, 2026, for judgment in a suit filed by Dr. Sani Abdullahi Shinkafi challenging the conduct of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Zamfara North Senatorial primary election. Justice Hassan Dikko fixed the date on Friday after parties in the matter adopted their final written addresses before the court. Shinkafi, an APC senatorial aspirant, had instituted the suit against the APC, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), and Senator Sahabi Ya’u over alleged irregularities in the party’s Zamfara North Senatorial primary election. Speaking after the proceedings, counsel to the plaintiff, Bello Galadi, said the matter was brought before the court for the adoption of final written addresses by all parties. Galadi explained that the plaintiff and the three other defendants successfully adopted their respective addresses, following which the court adjourned the matter for judgment. He expressed confidence that the court would deliver a fair and just judgment based on the merits of the case. “Today was set aside for the adoption of final written addresses, and all the parties have adopted their written addresses before the court. The matter has now been adjourned to August 31, 2026, for judgment,” he said. The presiding judge, who participated in the proceedings virtually, fixed the judgment date after all parties completed the adoption of their final written submissions. items.title: FA issues new rules on pitchside walls after ex-Arsenal player’s death
items.description: English football chiefs have announced new safety rules covering brick and concrete perimeter walls following the death of former Arsenal youth player Billy Vigar. The Chichester City forward, 21, died after suffering a brain injury in a match at Wingate and Finchley, in north London, in September 2025. It is believed the injury was caused when he collided with a concrete barrier. The Football Association (FA) carried out a safety review and has published new guidance for lower-league clubs which “no longer permits solid brick, breeze block or concrete barriers around pitches”. The ruling applies to clubs competing in the National League System for men (steps 1-6) and the Women’s National League (tiers 3-4). “Any existing solid brick, breeze block or concrete barriers must be removed as soon as reasonably practicable, or covered with suitable protection if they cannot be removed for structural reasons,” the FA said on Friday. “We have informed the clubs at this level that will be required to take action as a result of these changes.” AFP The post FA issues new rules on pitchside walls after ex-Arsenal player’s death appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: La crise de Sebta s'invite au Congrès espagnol : quatre ministres entendus fin août
items.description: Plusieurs ministres du gouvernement espagnol se présenteront devant le Congrès pour aborder les événements migratoires de la ville de Sebta occupée. Parmi eux se trouvent les ministre de l'intérieur, des Affaires étrangères et de la Défense. Dès vendredi, les ministres espagnols de l'Intérieur, Fernando Grande-Marlaska, des Affaires étrangères, José Manuel Albares, de la Défense, Margarita Robles et le ministre de la Justice, Félix Bolaños, déposeront une demande pour comparaitre devant le Parlement à leur initiative pour expliquer la crise de Sebta où 40.000 personnes ont tenté d'entrer de manière irrégulière à la nage. Selon des sources ministérielles citées par l'agence Europa Press, le gouvernement ibérique proposera une comparution de la ministre de la Défense le 25 août, celui de la Justice le 27 août, et les ministres de l'Intérieur et des Affaires étrangères le 28 août. Les comparutions devraient se faire devant des commissions spécialisées, à savoir celles de l'Intérieur, des Affaires étrangères, de la Défense et de la Sécurité nationale, précise la même source, afin de fournir des explications, répondre aux questions des députés, dans le cadre de leurs compétences. The post La crise de Sebta s'invite au Congrès espagnol : quatre ministres entendus fin août appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Ziguinchor : plusieurs têtes de bétail foudroyées par un poste électrique
items.description: Après la mort de plusieurs animaux de grande valeur dans le quartier Djéfaye, les éleveurs dénoncent un danger qui menace désormais autant leur cheptel que les habitants. ZIGUINCHOR – Le danger n’a pas frappé un être humain cette fois-ci. Cependant, il a laissé derrière lui un lourd préjudice et ravivé les inquiétudes. À Djéfaye, un quartier situé non loin du stade Aline Sitoé Diatta, dans la commune de Ziguinchor, un poste électrique à haute tension est au cœur d’un incident qui a coûté la vie à plusieurs têtes de bétail en l’espace de deux jours, entre mercredi et jeudi 06 août. Selon des témoignages recueillis, c’est une chèvre qui a été électrocutée en premier. Le lendemain, vers 17 heures, un taureau de race Holstein et une vache gestante appartenant à un membre de la Coopérative des Éleveurs du Sud ont subi le même sort. Les pertes sont considérables, avec un préjudice évalué entre trois et quatre millions F Cfa. Pour Moussa Sané, président de la Coopérative des éleveurs du Sud, le problème dépasse largement les pertes économiques. « Les animaux peuvent être remplacés. Mais si rien n’est fait, ce sont des vies humaines qui risquent d'être emportées. Chaque jour, cette zone est traversée par des piétons, des jeunes qui se rendent au stade et de nombreux véhicules », fustige-t-il. A lire aussi : Ziguinchor : un réseau de trafic de migrants vers les Canaries démantelé, six personnes déférées Face à cette situation, les éleveurs exhortent la Senelec à intervenir rapidement. « Nous demandons une vérification complète des installations et leur sécurisation, avant, pendant et après l’hivernage, afin d’éviter qu’un tel drame ne se reproduise », plaide Moussa Sané. Cet incident survient alors que la Coopérative des éleveurs du Sud multiplie les initiatives pour développer la filière, à travers des campagnes de vaccination du cheptel et un projet d’aménagement du site de Djifanghor. Ses responsables estiment toutefois que les éleveurs du Sud restent insuffisamment soutenus. Ils appellent l’État à renforcer son accompagnement financier et structurel afin de protéger les investissements, stimuler la production locale et réduire la dépendance aux importations de bétail, particulièrement à l’approche des grandes fêtes religieuses comme la Tabaski. Gaustin DIATTA (Correspondant)

items.title: Nigeria, Benin strengthen joint front against terrorism, cross-border crimes
items.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Nigeria and the Republic of Benin have renewed their commitment to strengthening regional security cooperation and combating terrorism, piracy and other cross-border crimes following a three-day working visit by the Minister of Defence, Gen. Christopher Gwabin Musa (rtd), to Cotonou. The visit focused on deepening bilateral defence relations, harmonising regional security frameworks and developing joint strategies to address emerging security threats across West Africa. During the visit, Gen. Musa called for greater coordination among regional security blocs to effectively respond to evolving security challenges, while urging regional forces to reaffirm their commitment to protecting democratic governance, securing land borders and safeguarding the Gulf of Guinea against maritime crimes. Hosted by his Beninese counterpart, Minister of National Defence, Mr. Gildas Agonkan, the Nigerian delegation secured commitments aimed at improving intelligence sharing, border security and operational cooperation between both countries. Reaffirming Nigeria’s zero-tolerance stance against terrorism, Gen. Musa urged Benin to work closely with Nigeria to prevent violent extremist groups from establishing footholds along their shared borders. He said Nigeria’s security forces remained determined to confront terrorists, bandits and other criminal elements threatening the peace of both countries. To strengthen border security, Nigeria offered to support measures that would enable security personnel to operate more effectively around border areas in order to prevent insurgent infiltration and illegal trafficking. A statement by the Ministry of Defence said both countries agreed to establish seamless, real-time intelligence-sharing mechanisms to enable their militaries to track and disrupt transnational criminal networks and insurgent groups before they carry out attacks. “The actionable intelligence pipeline will allow both militaries to track, trace and neutralise transnational criminal networks and insurgent cells before they execute operations,” the statement said. During the visit, Gen. Musa and his delegation inspected the Centre for Post Conflict De-mining and Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) Operations (CPADD) and the Glo-Djigbe Industrial Zone (GDIZ). The visits were aimed at promoting local capacity development in line with the third pillar of the minister’s defence agenda — intelligence-driven and technology-enabled defence. The engagements also provided an opportunity for both countries to exchange ideas on industrial development and economic cooperation in line with ECOWAS trade protocols and the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA). Gen. Musa also visited Nigerian Army troops deployed at Togbin, Cotonou, under the Peace Support Mission in Benin Republic, known as Operation ATILEYIN ALAFIA II. While addressing the troops, the minister praised their efforts and reiterated Nigeria’s commitment to working with Beninese forces to tackle terrorism and criminal activities. “We are going to partner with the troops of the Republic of Benin to ensure that we stop all those bandits and criminals that are killing people in our countries, so that we can deal with them,” he said. He explained that his visit was aimed at strengthening operational coordination between both countries to prevent criminals from exploiting border areas. The minister assured the troops that the Federal Government remained committed to improving their welfare and providing the necessary support to enable them carry out their duties. “We know our job is very, very difficult, and most times people don’t appreciate what we are doing. But God knows we are doing our best, and we are securing Nigeria,” he said. During the visit, Gen. Musa also held discussions with Nigeria’s Ambassador to Benin Republic, Mrs. Mopelola Ibrahim, reaffirming President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s commitment to military welfare and regional peace. The minister has since returned to Abuja after the successful completion of the visit. items.title: PTDF unveils strategy to support Nigeria’s $1trn GDP target
items.description: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja The Petroleum Technology Development Fund (PTDF) has unveiled a human capital development strategy aimed at supporting the Federal Government’s target of growing Nigeria’s economy to $1 trillion by 2030 through investment in specialised education, technical skills and energy research. The Executive Secretary of PTDF, Prof. Shua’ibu Aliyu, disclosed this on Friday in Kaduna, saying the Fund was aligning its programmes with the 2026–2030 National Development Plan to develop a highly skilled workforce capable of driving growth across Nigeria’s oil, gas and emerging energy sectors. Aliyu said the strategy focuses on building local capacity, reducing capital flight, strengthening research institutions and providing the manpower required for major energy infrastructure projects. “Our long-term vision is to develop a workforce that is trained in Nigeria, employed in Nigeria, and, by choice, exported to serve the broader African energy industry,” he said. He explained that the initiative would be implemented through two flagship institutions — the Centre for Skills Development and Training in Port Harcourt and the newly renamed General Shehu Musa Yar’Adua University of Geological Science and Engineering Technology in Kaduna. According to him, the Port Harcourt centre would provide internationally recognised vocational and technical training for technicians, artisans and craftsmen in the upstream, midstream and downstream petroleum sectors, with certifications in areas such as welding, fabrication, instrumentation and offshore safety. He added that the Kaduna-based university, recently licensed by the National Universities Commission (NUC) to operate as a postgraduate institution, would provide advanced education and research opportunities through partnerships with leading universities in the United Kingdom. Aliyu described the institution as “a strategic catalyst for Nigeria’s economic growth” through the development of local technical expertise and conservation of foreign exchange. To reduce dependence on overseas education, the PTDF boss said the Fund had expanded its split-site doctoral programme, allowing scholars to complete part of their studies in Nigeria and the remainder at partner universities abroad. “This initiative reduces capital flight while strengthening local institutions and maintaining international academic standards,” he said. He disclosed that PTDF was also digitising the university to improve administrative efficiency and support blended learning. The Executive Secretary said the Fund had aligned its training programmes with major national energy projects, including the AKK Gas Pipeline, UTM Floating LNG, Trans-Saharan Gas Pipeline, Bonga Southwest Aparo, Owowo, Zabazaba-Etan, OB3 Gas Trunk Line, Olokola LNG, Dangote projects and other investments by indigenous operators. He said the move was aimed at ensuring Nigeria develops the skilled workforce needed to execute future investments across the energy value chain. Aliyu added that PTDF was strengthening international partnerships with organisations such as the Independent Petroleum Producers Group, African Petroleum Producers’ Organization (APPO), Sonatrach of Algeria, Saudi Aramco and Turkish Petroleum to promote knowledge transfer, research and innovation. To reposition its academic institutions, he said PTDF had inaugurated a nine-member committee to review the university system, assess governance, infrastructure, research capacity, digital systems and academic programmes, and recommend reforms that would transform the institution into a globally competitive centre of excellence in petroleum, energy and strategic technology. The PTDF chief attributed the Fund’s achievements to the support of President Bola Tinubu, particularly the recent renaming of the university, which he said demonstrated the administration’s commitment to developing Nigeria’s energy workforce. Chairman of the review committee, Dr Omar Farouk Ibrahim, assured that the panel would carry out its assignment diligently and provide recommendations capable of transforming the institution. items.title: 2027: APC has failed Nigerians, ADC chieftain tells Tinubu, Mbah
items.description: By Anayo Okoli ENUGU — A chieftain of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Enugu State, Dr. (Sir) Walter Oji, has criticised the All Progressives Congress (APC) administration, alleging that the party has failed Nigerians and would struggle to secure victory in the 2027 general elections. Oji, a Fourth Degree Knight of the Catholic Church, made the remarks during the inaugural meeting of the G24 for Atiku Abubakar and Ocho Obodoeze 2027 Movement, an ADC support group, in Enugu. He claimed that the APC-led government had worsened economic hardship, insecurity and poverty in the country, arguing that Nigerians would demand a change of leadership in 2027. According to him, the ruling party had not delivered enough to justify another term in office. “It is time to tell Bola Tinubu that Nigerians deserve a new direction and that Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, a man with experience in governance and economic management, should be given the opportunity to lead the country in 2027,” Oji said. He also criticised Enugu State Governor Peter Mbah’s administration, alleging that some of its policies had increased the economic burden on residents. Oji urged residents of the state to support the ADC governorship candidate, Chief Ocho Obodoeze, ahead of the 2027 election. “I urge the people of Enugu State to support a new vision that prioritises development, prosperity and good governance,” he said. The ADC chieftain commended the organisers of the event for mobilising support for Atiku Abubakar, Ocho Obodoeze and other party candidates ahead of the 2027 elections. He, however, advised support groups not to rely solely on funding from the party or candidates but to mobilise resources from their members, stakeholders and supporters. Oji urged the groups to focus on grassroots mobilisation and communicate what he described as the party’s message of hope to Nigerians. He said citizens had the power to influence the direction of the country through their votes and called for greater participation in the democratic process. Among those present at the event were the Special Assistant to Atiku Abubakar on Special Duties, Dr. Ekene Onwuka; representative of the ADC presidential candidate’s wife, Anie Gift; ADC South-East Zonal Vice Chairman, Bon Unachukwu; and the Enugu State Caretaker Chairman, Gen. Chris Eze (rtd.). The post 2027: APC has failed Nigerians, ADC chieftain tells Tinubu, Mbah appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: PETROSOL secures approval to raise capital on Ghana Stock Exchange
items.description: PETROSOL Platinum Energy PLC, one of the leading oil marketing companies has received approval from the Ghana Stock Exchange and the Securities and Exchange Commission to raise long-term capital through the Ghana Stock Exchange, Managing Director Michael Bozumbil said. The approval marks a milestone for the company, which has evolved over two decades from a petroleum consulting firm into an indigenous oil marketing company in Ghana. “After a thorough assessment of PETROSOL’s business, including our governance systems, our compliance level, our credibility and growth plans, the Ghana Stock Exchange and the Securities and Exchange Commission have approved our request to raise patient capital on the stock exchange for our growth,” Bozumbil said at the Ghana International Petroleum Conference in Accra. He said the proceeds would fund the company’s long-term expansion strategy, including investments in renewable energy, solar power and electric vehicle charging infrastructure. “We have a clear plan to grow sustainably. We will continue to look for opportunities and the right partnerships to invest in the energy sector through innovation while taking advantage of government policies to expand our operations and deliver clean, long-lasting fuel and renewable energy solutions to our customers,” he said. Founded in 2006 as a petroleum business management and consulting firm, PETROSOL entered the oil marketing business in 2014, benefiting from government policies aimed at increasing indigenous participation in Ghana’s downstream petroleum sector. The company now operates more than 100 fuel stations across Ghana and employs about 490 people. Bozumbil attributed PETROSOL’s growth to corporate governance, prudent financial management and regulatory compliance despite challenging economic conditions. He said the company has obtained three International Organization for Standardization (ISO) certifications covering quality management, occupational health and safety, and environmental management. It has also received recognition from the Ghana Revenue Authority for tax compliance and remains in good standing with the National Petroleum Authority, the Environmental Protection Agency and the Ghana Standards Authority. Beyond its petroleum business, PETROSOL is investing in renewable energy and plans to install electric vehicle charging stations at selected service stations as part of Ghana’s energy transition. Bozumbil said policy consistency remains critical to enabling indigenous companies to compete with multinational firms in Ghana’s downstream petroleum sector. “As an indigenous company that has benefited from the consistent implementation of government policies promoting the growth of indigenous private companies, we believe collaboration and policy consistency are critical to building a resilient downstream petroleum industry,” he said. He said PETROSOL’s sponsorship of the 2026 Ghana International Petroleum Conference reflected its commitment to supporting industry dialogue and encouraging innovation, investment and sustainable growth. Looking ahead, Bozumbil said the company would continue expanding its retail fuel network, growing its renewable energy business and creating jobs. “We will continue to invest for growth. PETROSOL will remain a value-for-money brand, a good corporate citizen and an employer of choice. We will continue to energise dreams, ignite hope and power individuals and businesses to achieve their aspirations in an environmentally sustainable and ethical manner,” he said. The planned capital raise is expected to strengthen PETROSOL’s financial position and broaden investment opportunities in Ghana’s capital market, the company said.

items.title: Osun Election: Reps minority caucus raises alarm over alleged intimidation
items.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The Minority Caucus of the House of Representatives has raised concerns over what it described as alleged intimidation of the Osun State Government ahead of next week’s governorship election. In a statement jointly signed on Friday by the Minority Leader, Hon. Fredrick Agbedi, and the Caucus Spokesman, Hon. Afam Victor Ogene, the lawmakers criticised President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s directive to the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) to vacate the order freezing the state’s accounts, describing it as an “afterthought.” The caucus argued that the President’s intervention came only after public criticism of the EFCC’s action, adding that it raised questions over the legality of the initial decision. The lawmakers cited comments attributed to EFCC spokesman Wilson Uwujaren that the accounts were frozen without a valid court order, noting that the President later directed the commission to approach the court to vacate the order. The caucus questioned the conflicting explanations surrounding the issue, asking whether a court order existed at the time the accounts were frozen and whether the President was fully aware of the actions of his appointees. The lawmakers also alleged a pattern of actions by the Federal Government that they claimed amounted to pressure on Osun State ahead of the election. They cited the alleged withholding of statutory allocations meant for local governments in the state, describing it as a move capable of affecting grassroots administration. The caucus further alleged that political violence involving some supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC) and other groups had continued in the state, accusing security agencies of failing to respond adequately. It also criticised the arrest and detention of the Secretary to the Osun State Government, Teslim Igbalaiye, and others, describing the development as an attack on the state government’s institution. The lawmakers faulted the conduct of the Osun State Commissioner of Police and expressed concern over allegations made after the Inspector-General of Police’s visit to the state that the government was harbouring suspected criminals. “This is not policing. It is partisan propaganda in uniform,” the caucus said. The opposition lawmakers warned that the actions of some government officials could affect public confidence in the administration. “The mask is off. Nigerians can now see clearly that the APC has weaponised federal institutions against opposition states — a dress rehearsal of what is to come in the 2027 general elections,” the statement added. The caucus called on relevant stakeholders to ensure that Osun residents are allowed to exercise their voting rights freely and without intimidation. “The people of Osun should be given the enabling environment to freely exercise their constitutional right to vote, without fear, coercion or voter apathy,” it said. It urged civil society organisations and the international community to closely monitor developments before, during and after the election, while calling for accountability in the event of any breach of peace. “Osun people will vote. Osun people will be protected. And democracy will prevail,” the statement concluded. items.title: AI must empower entrepreneurs, not replace human creativity – UPS Global Director
items.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) should be viewed as a tool for strengthening entrepreneurship rather than replacing human creativity and critical thinking, Global Director of Social Impact at UPS, La’Kerri Jackson, has said. Speaking at the opening of a two-day entrepreneurship workshop in Accra on Thursday, Ms Jackson encouraged business owners to embrace AI as a practical tool for improving productivity while continuing to rely on their knowledge, experience and innovation. The workshop, organised by the International Trade Centre’s (ITC) SheTrades Initiative in partnership with UPS, Visa and the Ghana Export Promotion Authority (GEPA), has brought together 200 established and aspiring Ghanaian entrepreneurs. It is designed to build participants’ skills in artificial intelligence, digital payments, logistics, marketing and access to finance. According to Ms Jackson, entrepreneurs worldwide face similar challenges, particularly limited access to capital and export opportunities. She said this made collaboration between development partners and the private sector essential. “There are many challenges that entrepreneurs and small businesses face, from exporting challenges to the lack of access to capital. It’s not just specific to Ghana; it’s all over the globe,” she said. She noted that UPS works with organisations worldwide to help entrepreneurs overcome these barriers through training, mentorship and access to business support networks. Among the partnerships she highlighted were collaborations with Opportunity International to provide interest-free, collateral-free microloans; the Fearless Fund to support business growth; and the International Trade Centre to equip entrepreneurs with practical skills and resources. A key focus of the Accra workshop is helping small business owners understand how AI can be applied to their daily operations without requiring advanced technical expertise. Ms Jackson said many entrepreneurs already had access to free digital tools that could help improve their businesses. “It’s not as hard as we think it is. There are practical tools available through platforms like WhatsApp and Instagram for marketing, creating flyers and promoting businesses without investing a lot of money,” she said. She, however, cautioned entrepreneurs against becoming overly dependent on AI, stressing that technology should complement, rather than replace, human judgement. “The angle that people should take is that AI is a thought-leadership partner. You are the brands. You have the intellect. You have the intellectual property,” she said. “There is a danger in becoming so dependent on it, but everybody has to exercise discipline and continue to lean on their own intellect.” Also addressing participants, UPS Foundation Manager Bassen Anari challenged entrepreneurs to translate the lessons from the workshop into practical business actions. He observed that although many entrepreneurs enthusiastically participated in training programmes, only a few went on to implement what they had learnt.

items.title: Burkina: Les demandes d’agréments et de conventions au ministère de la Santé désormais sur « e-Agrément »
items.description: Burkina: Les demandes d’agréments et de conventions au ministère de la Santé désormais sur « e-Agrément » Ouagadougou, 7 août 2026 (AIB)- Le ministre de la Santé a officiellement lancé, vendredi à Ouagadougou, la plateforme « e-Agrément », destinée à simplifier et à accélérer les procédures de demande d’ouverture et d’exploitation des établissements privés de santé et les demandes de convention avec le ministère. Accessible à l’adresse https://e-agrement.minsante.bf/, la plateforme permet aux usagers de créer un compte, de choisir la procédure souhaitée, de renseigner le formulaire et de téléverser les pièces justificatives directement en ligne. Selon le directeur du Système d’information du ministère de la Santé, Dimitri Ouattara la plateforme est opérationnelle depuis fin avril 2026. Elle avait déjà enregistré, à la date du lancement officiel, 247 demandes, dont 39 ont abouti à une autorisation. « Avant, on avait une procédure en plus de 16 étapes », a-t-il expliqué, soulignant que la dématérialisation permet désormais aux usagers de suivre l’évolution de leurs dossiers en temps réel, sans avoir à effectuer de multiples déplacements. Le système permet également aux différents services habilités du ministère d’examiner les dossiers et de formuler leurs recommandations sur une même plateforme. Cette organisation devrait améliorer la traçabilité des dossiers et réduire les risques de perte de documents, tout en contribuant à raccourcir les délais de traitement, a ajouté le DSI. Le ministre de la Santé, Dr Robert Lucien Jean-Claude Kargougou, a présenté « e-Agrément » comme une première étape vers la création d’un « guichet unique de la santé » pour les procédures administratives qui seront progressivement dématérialisées. Il a rappelé qu’avant la mise en place de la plateforme, l’obtention d’une autorisation d’ouverture d’une formation sanitaire privée nécessitait 16 étapes et l’intervention de 11 intermédiaires. « Avec cette plateforme l’accès aux services devient beaucoup plus allégé, il y a beaucoup plus de transparence, beaucoup plus de simplification et beaucoup plus de traçabilité », a déclaré le ministre, invitant les professionnels de santé, les organisations de la société civile et les partenaires techniques et financiers à s’approprier la plateforme. La ministre en charge de la Transition digitale Aminata Zerbo/Sabane a, pour sa part, indiqué que ce lancement s’inscrit dans la dynamique gouvernementale d’accélération de la dématérialisation des services et procédures de l’administration publique. Elle a salué l’engagement du ministère de la Santé, qui mène également d’autres chantiers de transformation numérique, notamment la dématérialisation des licences d’affaires et la mise en place du système d’information hospitalier. « Ce sont des plateformes qui permettront en tout cas d’améliorer la qualité des services rendus à ces populations », a-t-elle affirmé, estimant que ces outils contribueront également à rendre l’administration sanitaire plus efficace. Parmi les premiers bénéficiaires de la plateforme figure l’ONG Jibayo, qui a obtenu une convention d’appui avec le ministère de la Santé. Son directeur pays, le Dr Jérémy Zoulana, a indiqué que la procédure, entamée en mai, a été finalisée en moins de trois mois. Il a expliqué que son organisation a pu créer son compte, renseigner les informations demandées et transmettre les pièces justificatives en ligne, tout en recevant régulièrement des informations sur l’état d’avancement du dossier. Selon lui, cette expérience contraste avec les procédures antérieures effectuées sur support papier, qui pouvaient prendre « autour d’une année », notamment en raison des risques de perte ou d’erreur dans les documents. Le Dr Zoulana a toutefois relevé que les difficultés rencontrées étaient principalement liées à la connexion internet et non au fonctionnement de la plateforme, ajoutant que son organisation a bénéficié d’une assistance des responsables du ministère tout au long de la procédure. À travers « e-Agrément », le ministère de la Santé entend ainsi poursuivre la modernisation de ses procédures administratives et faciliter l’accès des usagers à ses services. Agence d’information du Burkina YOS/ata
